legend.0: The execution path is straightforward and local.
legend.1: Following a path requires tracking several branches or state changes.
legend.2: Following a path requires repeatedly connecting distant branches and changing state.

legend.0: No meaningful duplication; repeated structure is limited to trivial declarations or accessors.
legend.1: A few small blocks repeat with minor variations.
legend.2: Several substantial blocks repeat so that a behavior change would require editing multiple copies.
legend.3: Most of the logic is copied with variations, and the copies have already diverged or contain inconsistencies.

legend.0: State is held in one authoritative place, or the code is effectively stateless.
legend.1: One piece of state is cached or mirrored, and it is invalidated or updated at a single clear point.
legend.2: Several values are mirrored or cached, and keeping them consistent depends on every writer remembering to update each copy or flag.
legend.3: Mirrored or cached state is updated inconsistently in the visible code, so some paths can leave the copies out of sync.

legend.0: Related elements are held in arrays, collections, or objects and are processed generically; there is no hand enumeration.
legend.1: A small set of related elements is spelled out by hand in one or two places, and adding an element would touch only those places.
legend.2: A larger set of related elements is spelled out by hand in several methods, so adding or changing an element requires editing each method that enumerates them.
legend.3: Almost every method enumerates a large set of related elements by hand, with long hand-written expressions or key lists where one omitted or misordered element would be hard to notice.
